# bugs #4145: SIGSEGV for an expression that combines a run-time value with a constexpr object

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/4145/
- Category: [Fixes](../../fix.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Apply the patch and close. It has the two guards of the patch attached to the ticket and a third one.
- Patch: [bugs-4145.patch](../../patches/bugs-4145.patch), commit [`3757ac76b`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/3757ac76b011913d11899d3b470c688e2dddb91a). Applies to r17176 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

With `constexpr int c = 3;` and a variable `x`, the compiler terminates with SIGSEGV for the
expression `x + c`. This was reproduced for mcs51 for `x + c`, `x ? 4 : c`, `(x, c)`, and
`a[x + c]`. C99 code is affected as well. The compiler crashes for `x + (int){3}`, because a
compound literal with a constant initializer is implicitly `constexpr`.

## Cause

The `constexpr` marker is stored in the type specifier, so an expression that is computed from a
`constexpr` object inherits the marker through its type. `propagateConstExpr` and
`constExprValue` in `src/SDCCast.c` treat every node with the marker as the object and read
`AST_SYMBOL (...)->ival`. An operator node has no symbol. `typeofOp` copies the marker to an
object that is declared with `typeof` or `auto` from such an expression, and that object is then
`constexpr` without a constant initializer.

## Fix

`constExprValue` and `propagateConstExpr` require a symbol node (`IS_AST_SYM_VALUE`) before they
read the initializer. `typeofOp` clears the marker when its operand is not a symbol node. The
patch attached to the ticket has the first two guards. The change to `typeofOp` is additional.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-4145.c` has 36 assertions. They cover arithmetic, shift, bitwise,
comparison, conditional, and comma operators, an array index, `auto` and `typeof`, objects of type
`int` and `long`, and the compound literal forms. `support/valdiag/tests/bug-4145.c` has four
cases. Three check that such an expression is rejected where a constant expression is required,
and one compiles `typeof` and `auto` declarations.

Without the patch the regression test does not compile for mcs51. With the patch it passes on the
host, for six mcs51 configurations (the four models, and small and large with `--stack-auto`), for
stm8, and for z80. valdiag has no failures for mcs51, mcs51-large, and mcs51-stack-auto. The
regression suite for mcs51-small has no failures, and no other test changes its code size.

## Related

The patch does not fix these problems:

- `typeof (c)` and `auto y = c`, where `c` is a `constexpr` object or a compound literal with a
  constant initializer, make the new object `constexpr`. Errors 2 and 33 follow.
- `case c:` with a `constexpr` object `c` gets error 62.
- A compound literal inside the body of a `switch` statement is initialized at the start of the
  switch block. That code is never executed, so the literal has a wrong value when it is read. The
  compiler prints warnings 126 and 84.
